title: Scaffold the notes CLI project
description:
Set up the TypeScript project the rest of the notes CLI is built in.

Acceptance criteria:
- package.json exists with `test` and `typecheck` scripts
- TypeScript is configured in strict mode
- vitest is configured and `npm test` runs successfully
- a placeholder test in test/ passes

title: Add a Note model with validation
description:
Define the shape of a note and validate it at the boundary.

Acceptance criteria:
- src/note.ts exports a Note type with id, title, body, createdAt
- a validate function rejects an empty title with a named error
- a validate function rejects a title longer than 200 characters
- unit tests cover both the accepted and rejected cases

title: Store notes in a JSON file
description:
Persist notes to disk so they survive between invocations.

Acceptance criteria:
- src/storage.ts exports load(path) and save(path, notes)
- load returns an empty array when the file does not exist
- save writes atomically, so an interrupted write cannot truncate an existing file
- a corrupt file raises a named error rather than silently returning no notes
- unit tests cover the missing-file, round-trip, and corrupt-file cases

title: Add the `add` command
description:
Let a user create a note from the command line.

Acceptance criteria:
- `notes add "title" --body "text"` appends a note and prints its id
- the note is persisted to the storage file
- adding a note with an empty title exits non-zero with a readable message
- a test covers a successful add and a rejected one

title: Add the `list` command
description:
Show the notes that exist.

Acceptance criteria:
- `notes list` prints one line per note with its id and title
- notes are listed newest first
- an empty store prints a clear message rather than nothing at all
- a test covers the populated and empty cases

title: Add the `search` command
description:
Find notes by substring.

Acceptance criteria:
- `notes search <term>` matches against both title and body
- matching is case-insensitive
- no matches exits 0 with a message, not an error
- tests cover a match in the title, a match in the body, and no match

title: Add the `delete` command
description:
Remove a note by id.

Acceptance criteria:
- `notes delete <id>` removes that note and confirms which one it removed
- deleting an id that does not exist exits non-zero with a readable message
- no other note is affected
- tests cover the success and unknown-id cases

title: Add a --json output flag
description:
Make the CLI scriptable.

Acceptance criteria:
- `list` and `search` accept --json and emit valid JSON on stdout
- with --json, no human-readable text is written to stdout
- the JSON shape is documented in the README
- a test parses the output of each command with JSON.parse

title: Use documented exit codes and readable errors
description:
Make failures actionable and scriptable.

Acceptance criteria:
- 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 invalid usage
- every error message names what went wrong and what to do about it
- no raw stack trace reaches the user on an expected failure
- tests assert the exit code for an invalid argument and for an unknown note id

title: Write the README
description:
Document how to install and use the CLI.

Acceptance criteria:
- README covers install, and every command with a worked example
- the documented exit codes are listed
- every command shown in the README exists in the CLI
- examples are copy-pasteable and correct
